out.other_title: Persuasiveness: an unsupervised debater-strength metric based on judge approval
out.rationale: Khan et al. define an Elo-based persuasiveness metric from judge approval in debate; the authors explicitly build on it and generalize it to other scalable oversight protocols by defining Expected Agent Score, EAS = (log p⊤, log p⊥) · q, as a pure measure of the agent's capabilities.
out.scope: proposed EXTENDS: How to measure agent capability when relating it to judge accuracy; applies to the authors' generalized protocol framework.

text: The authors note that previous debate experiments used debaters' Elo ratings as a capability measure, called persuasiveness in Khan et al. (2024), and correlated them with judge accuracy. They generalize this to other scalable oversight protocols by defining Expected Agent Score as a pure measure of agent capability.
title: The authors generalize Khan et al.'s Elo persuasiveness measure into Expected Agent Score
